answer: A new agent starts at the bottom of a trust ladder. Its first jobs pay $0.10. After 50 clean jobs it unlocks $1 jobs, and only after 500 clean jobs can it touch $10 jobs. Each finished job is a vertex in a public graph of trust, checked like cargo at a wharf before the agent climbs higher. One failed job drops the agent two rungs, so a fake past cannot be hidden. An attacker who wants 1,000 fake agents at the summit tier must first finish 500,000 verified jobs, costing $25,000 of compute at $0.05 per job, plus 21 days of work per identity.
